work: Larry Hurtado's Blog, post 'The Origin of “Divine Christology”?', 2017-10-09
chapter_or_section: post body, paragraph beginning "Second, critical analysis"
page: page unknown (blog post, no print pagination)
quote_orig: Second, critical analysis of the historical traditions does not yield evidence that Jesus himself actually claimed to share in divine glory and status during his earthly career. [footnote marker omitted] Instead, the classic instances where Jesus makes such claims for himself are scenes where the risen/exalted Jesus speaks, e.g., Matthew 28:16-20; Luke 24:44-52.
context_before: Hurtado answers Loke's book on the origin of divine Christology; this is his stated historical position.
what_it_says: Hurtado states that critical analysis of the historical traditions finds no evidence that the earthly Jesus claimed divine status, and that the Gospel scenes of such claims are risen-Jesus scenes.
claim_supported: (E) Hurtado denies, for the historical Jesus, the claim (A) that Jesus himself claimed to be YHWH; cites risen-Jesus scenes instead.
scholar_qualification: He says the early basis for high Christology was what God claimed and demanded (resurrection and exaltation), and he separates that historical question from theological validity.
limits: Footnote marker [i] removed between the two sentences (marked in the quote); footnote [i] itself not read in full. Comment thread not used here. Blog post not a PDF, so no page image.
